spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶1:** [GAP-1: REVIEW The] whole of the lust to seize and corrupt what belongs to the good — this is the original proprium of self-love that first arose within the states of utter falsity and evil.

**¶2:** Within this consuming lust that [GAP-2: ...] within it, the Divine Celestial Human who descended into the realm of falsity [GAP-3: ...] its destructive falsity from evil [GAP-4: ...] its malice. The external truths that clothed him were [GAP-5: ...] evil severed them from their source and drew them out; [GAP-6: ...]

**¶3:** It lusted after the divine human form of the Emissary of Wisdom, which he revealed to it from celestial states above, in the likeness of the Divine that it perceived. It fixed a counterfeit form — an imprint of the divine likeness fashioned from the merely natural proprium — and stamped the reflection of that divine form onto its own selfhood, which was entirely its own production from evil.

**¶4:** For the third time it lusted after the most ancient celestial humanity. It seized a living faculty from that celestial state, and brought it forth from a [GAP-7: REVIEW — the innermost proprial capacity of] the most ancient celestial humanity's [GAP-8: REVIEW — natural will and selfhood], separating from that celestial wholeness a derived form that it could possess and dominate.

---
*Note on ¶3:* The "seal" and "image of flesh" correspond precisely to what Swedenborg describes as the phantasy of evil spirits fashioning an appearance of the human form from their own proprium — a simulacrum of the Divine Human made entirely from self-love, not from inflowing life. The "birth" is what the hells produce from themselves: counterfeit life.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: [The] entirety of envy is this first nature that occu[red] in the worlds of darkness.
In this envy that [existed] in it, the First Man [swallowed] its poiso[n and] its evil-doing. His garment[s] were [seized] it cut them and drew them; [ ... ]

It envied the first image of the Ambassador, which he displayed to it in the heights abov[e], i[n] his form that it saw. It established the seal and the image of flesh, and put the impression of t[h]at image on flesh, its very own birth.
[The th]ird time it envied Adam, the fir[st hum]an. It seized a power from him, and bore it forth from a [rib] of Adam's [flesh].

fills.explanation: The definite article is required to introduce "entirety of envy" as a defined concept; the spiritual reading confirms this opening.

A verb of presence/being is needed for "the envy that [verb] in it" (i.e., within darkness); "existed" fits the expository register of the Kephalaia and the spiritual reading's "consuming lust that [was] within it."

In Manichaean cosmology the First Man took in the poison of darkness during his descent into battle; "swallowed" is the standard Kephalaia term for this event and corresponds to the spiritual reading's description of the celestial human encountering destructive falsity.

Completes "poison" and provides the conjunction linking the parallel phrase "its poison and its evil-doing," matching the spiritual reading's pairing of "destructive falsity from evil" and "its malice."

The garments (external truths/five sons) of the First Man were seized by darkness, logically preceding the cutting and drawing described in the next clause; the spiritual reading confirms evil acted upon these truths before severing them.

The editor's core word "rib" is correct — it corresponds precisely to Swedenborg's exegesis of the proprium (AC 147–151) and the spiritual reading's "innermost proprial capacity" — but the trailing "of" must be dropped since "of" already appears in the visible text after the gap.

Confirmed: "flesh" corresponds to the natural will and selfhood (proprium) in Swedenborg (AC 148–149, 3813), matching the spiritual reading's "natural will and selfhood" and completing the Genesis 2:21 parallel of Eve fashioned from Adam's rib of flesh.
